clue.text: Bringing lads close to breakdown in Southern Spain

indicators.note: a breakdown leaves things in pieces, so these three words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone drives a group of young men to the edge of collapse while holidaying in the south of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakdown' is the anagram signal: rearrange LADS CLOSE TO. 'Bringing' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Costa del Sol is the coastal resort strip of Andalusia, on Spain's southern shore.

clue.text: Talk about city transport long superseded

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for talk goes around the city

parts.note: to talk casually is to chat
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city, often shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: Discussion about urban transport that has long been replaced by newer systems.
explanation.definitionFit: The chariot was an ancient horse-drawn war and racing vehicle, obsolete for millennia.

clue.text: Point to point say

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
a peak is a pointed summit or tip

explanation.surface: A phrase recalling point-to-point horse racing, followed by an invitation to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point to point' suggests the horse race; here it is S (a compass point) going to PEAK (a point).
explanation.definitionFit: To say something is to utter it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Union strike mounted in a contest without end

indicators.note: in tells us the turned word for strike sits inside the remaining letters
without end tells us to drop the last letter of the word for contest

parts.note: a game is a contest

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the word climbs upward, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to lam is to strike or thrash

explanation.surface: A trade union's strike is staged in the middle of an endless competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns LAM into MAL, which goes inside A + GAM (GAME losing its end, from 'without end').
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a mixture or combination, so it is a union of different things.

clue.text: The selfish creature is to get off

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone wrong or out of order signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-centred being announces that it is time to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal for IS TO GET.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotist is a self-absorbed person who thinks mainly of themselves.

clue.text: Makes clear charm's no longer pleasing

parts.note: read as charms, plural: magical charms are spells
something no longer in favour or fashionable is out

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a particular charm has lost its appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charm's' is read as the plural charms, giving SPELLS.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell out something is to explain it in plain, explicit detail.

clue.text: Pole possibly given ancient name

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word Pole might be arranged another way

parts.note: ancient means old

explanation.surface: A Polish man might have been given a name from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals an anagram of POLE, giving LEOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Leopold is a male given name, borne by several Belgian kings.

clue.text: Promenade with a game American lawyer

parts.note: a game leg is a lame one, so game can mean lame
DA, district attorney, a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: Strolling along with a sporting American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' here is the adjective meaning injured or crippled, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a public walk lined with trees, a word from Spanish.

clue.text: Pocket fitting

definitions.meaning: to pocket is to take for oneself, to seize

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to take possession of; as an adjective, suitable.

clue.text: Simple and single female, no longer young

parts.note: single means one
someone no longer young is old

explanation.surface: A description of an uncomplicated unmarried woman past her youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Onefold, an old word, means single in nature, hence uncomplicated or plain.

clue.text: Show bad spirit-the way to count!

parts.note: a demon is an evil spirit
ST, short for street, a way
to rate is to reckon or count as

explanation.surface: An evil spirit is shown the method of counting.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate is to display or prove by example.

clue.text: Groom appears right in a pretty colour

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for right is placed within the colour

parts.note: pink is a pretty colour

explanation.surface: A groom shows up at the wedding correctly dressed in pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' is a verb here: to tidy oneself. 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To prink is to dress up or primp, smartening one's appearance.

clue.text: Prepare to wrap up burn where meat's cooked at high heat

definitions.text: where meat's cooked at high heat

indicators.note: to wrap up means to enclose, so the stream goes inside the word for prepare

parts.note: to groom someone is to prepare them for a role
burn is a Scottish word for a stream, and a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Instructions to prepare and bandage a burn, oddly set in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burn' looks like a cooking or injury word; it is a Scottish stream, a RILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A grill-room is a restaurant or room specialising in grilled meats.

clue.text: Love work-out-one a mother finds best

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
PT, physical training, is a work-out
I, the Roman numeral for one
mum is a mother

explanation.surface: A mother decides that loving one particular exercise routine is best.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable condition, the ideal.

clue.text: Taken for a fit purpose

parts.note: reads as something done for a suitable reason, but means swallowed to treat a fit or seizure, as remedies are

explanation.definitionFit: Something medicinal has healing properties and is taken to cure an illness.

clue.text: Tend to be agitated about staff getting underfoot

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters surround the staff
agitated means stirred up, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Someone tends to get worked up about staff who keep getting in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be agitated' rearranges TEND as T + DEN, placed around ROD. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trodden has been walked on, pressed down by feet.

clue.text: A body of soldiers yields and retreats

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
cedes means gives up or yields

explanation.surface: A military unit gives ground and falls back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or withdraw.

clue.text: On the road, yet case is ill-organised

indicators.note: something badly arranged has its letters jumbled, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a legal case is still disorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-organised' rearranges YET CASE; 'is' is a link. Cat's-eyes are reflective studs set in road surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-eye is a reflector stud set into a road to mark lanes at night.

clue.text: A key should be held by the more morose cleaner

indicators.note: held by means kept inside, so the key goes within the word for more morose

parts.note: sourer means more sullen or morose
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: A gloomier person ought to keep hold of a key, perhaps for the cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourer is a pad or tool used for scrubbing pots clean.

clue.text: The person sick of being uncomplaining?

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is someone receiving medical treatment; as an adjective it means tolerant and forbearing.

clue.text: Quietly tell a man of the church

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to relate is to tell or narrate

explanation.surface: A request to speak softly to a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking cleric such as a bishop.

clue.text: Smart English worker encompassing support

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the support sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker
a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: A well-dressed English labourer surrounded by backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means stylish and well-dressed.

clue.text: Such food makes a hero tick!

indicators.note: the food's letters, rearranged, make the words given, so this is an anagram signal

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a particular vegetable is what drives a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram runs from answer to clue: the vegetable's letters can be rearranged to give A HERO TICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A globe artichoke is a vegetable whose fleshy bracts are eaten.

clue.text: The thanks expressed in a letter to a Greek

parts.note: ta is an informal British way of saying thanks

explanation.surface: Thanks are expressed in a letter to a man from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Your old-fashioned scrawny egghead

parts.note: scrawny means thin
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: Insulting someone as a dated, skinny intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' is not an intellectual but the head (first letter) of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Thine is the archaic possessive form meaning yours.

clue.text: Regal lady who got cross at every halt when late

definitions.text: Regal lady who got cross at every halt when late

parts.words: Regal lady who got cross at every halt when late
parts.note: sounds like a queen losing her temper, but refers to the stone crosses Edward I raised at each night's stop of his dead wife's funeral procession

explanation.definitionFit: Edward I's queen, Eleanor of Castile, is commemorated by the twelve Eleanor crosses marking her cortege's resting places.

clue.text: Put spirit into a friend content in retirement

indicators.note: content means contents, what is held inside, so the reversed word goes within

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: Cheering up a pal who is happy to be retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' is not happy but contents; 'retirement' turns IN into NI, which sits inside A MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to enliven or give life to.

clue.text: Producing Greenmantle? That's stretching it a bit!

indicators.note: the letters of the answer rearranged produce the novel's title, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A remark on producing an edition of John Buchan's thriller Greenmantle, with a jibe about exaggeration.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenmantle is a John Buchan spy novel. 'That's' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlargement is an increase in size, as when a photograph is blown up.
